best_for: Windows developers whose project or library still targets Python 3.13 and who want the classic python.org installer rather than the new install manager.
description:
Python is a general-purpose programming language, looked after by the Python Software Foundation, a nonprofit. This listing is the 3.13 release line, which python.org describes as a mix of changes to the language, the interpreter and the standard library. Several old library modules, deprecated since 3.11, were removed in it.

The most visible change is a new interactive shell. You can edit a block of several lines and get it back from history, type help, exit or quit without brackets, and see prompts and error tracebacks in color. F1 opens help, F2 browses history and F3 makes pasting big chunks of code easier. 3.13 also brings an experimental free-threaded mode and an early Just-In-Time compiler.

points.title: 3.13 is in security-only mode
points.text: Regular bug fix releases for 3.13 ended with 3.13.16 on October 1, 2026. From here, only security fixes come, as needed, until about October 2029.

points.title: Installers are winding down
points.text: Security releases are normally source only. 3.13.17 got Windows installers as an exception, and 3.13.18 was released without them. Expect 3.13.17 to be the last Windows installer unless that changes.

points.title: Newer Pythons use the install manager
points.text: On python.org, 3.14 and later are installed through the Python install manager. 3.13 is still offered as a regular installer and an embeddable zip.

points.title: Three architectures, two scopes
points.text: Installers are published for 64-bit, 32-bit and ARM64 Windows, and each can install for just you or for all users. python.org notes it cannot be used on Windows 7 or earlier.

points.title: Free and open
points.text: Python is free and open source under the PSF license, and python.org charges nothing for the installers.

points.title: Versions here
points.text: This site lists 3.13 for Windows only and keeps 18 versions, which helps when you need to match an exact patch release.
